clue.text: A male aboard pilot ship

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the A and male letters sit inside the word for pilot

parts.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it

explanation.surface: A man climbs aboard to guide a vessel through the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' looks like a noun but is the verb, giving STEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by steam power, the classic paddle or liner of old, is a type of ship.

clue.text: Carve sailing ship, first to be taken out

indicators.note: the opening letter of the sailing-ship word is removed, as the clue says the first is taken out

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Someone carves a model sailing ship, removing the first piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave a design by cutting into a surface is a synonym for carving it.

clue.text: Seat I must sit in daily

indicators.note: the letter I has to sit inside the word for a daily cleaner

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day

explanation.surface: Someone insists on their own seat, which they must sit in every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like an adverb but is a noun: in Britain a daily or char is a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of furniture with a back for one person to sit on is a seat.

clue.text: Initially, group of us restaurateurs encountered connoisseur of good food

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the four words that follow

parts.note: to have encountered someone is to have met them

explanation.surface: A party of restaurant owners meets a food critic.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure who appreciates fine cooking is exactly a connoisseur of good food.

clue.text: Catch number on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back says the number word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone catches a bus with a certain route number on the return trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap fish or a ball in a mesh is to catch it; the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Workers not working with complete ease

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farm hands
a computer system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: Idle workers seem to be taking things very easily.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for winning effortlessly, originally from a jockey relaxing his grip, means with complete ease.

clue.text: Energy needed to cross river in flow

indicators.note: the energy word spans the river letter, crossing over it so it sits inside

parts.note: steam is a source of energy, as in steam power

explanation.surface: Power is needed to get across a flowing river.
explanation.definitionFit: A continuous flow of water, people or data is a stream.

clue.text: Lizard again roaming around for all to see

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap round the film-rating letter
roaming means wandering about, so the letters of again move into a new order

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: A lizard is again wandering about in full view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts IGANA (the anagram of AGAIN) round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tropical American reptile is a kind of lizard.

clue.text: Favour country mansion in Memphis

parts.note: grace means favour, as in being in someone's good graces
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A country estate in Memphis is favoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's home in Memphis, Tennessee, is the famous mansion meant here.

clue.text: Short petty argument in health resort

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter of the quarrel word goes

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A brief, trivial quarrel breaks out at a health resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A town with mineral springs where people go to take the waters is a health resort.

clue.text: Extremely large bird, a kind having no tail

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: having no tail means the final letter of the kind word is dropped

parts.note: nice means kind

explanation.surface: An enormous bird, of a gentle kind, lacks its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gigantic, like the Titans of Greek myth, is extremely large.

clue.text: Learn, when out of sorts, about the kidneys

indicators.note: out of sorts means unsettled or disordered, so the letters of learn are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sick patient learns about their kidneys.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for anything relating to the kidneys, as in failure of that organ, is a medical term.

clue.text: Boast of British newspaper

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A British newspaper brags about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk boastfully about oneself is a synonym for boast.

clue.text: Allegiance shown the Stuarts, for example, when changing leaders?

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for kings and queens is swapped for a different one

parts.note: the Stuarts were a royal house, an example of royalty

explanation.surface: Loyalty was shown to the Stuart kings, as when the Jacobites backed a change of monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap puts L in place of the opening R; the playful 'changing leaders' also nods to the Stuarts losing the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness owed to a sovereign or cause is allegiance.

clue.text: Clairvoyance: supporter with view

parts.note: a second supports a boxer or duellist, or seconds a motion
a sight is a view

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant's backer has a vision.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed ability to see future or distant events is clairvoyance.

clue.text: Former player, demanding type

parts.note: ex means former
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A retired performer has a reputation for being demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who exacts, insisting on payment or obedience, is a demanding type.

clue.text: I was at the Hatter's tea party to protest over race

definitions.text: I was at the Hatter's tea party

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first word stands on top of the second

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
to hare is to race or run fast

explanation.surface: A guest at the Mad Hatter's tea party complains about a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a first-person riddle: the speaker is a character from Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's story, the guests at the Mad Hatter's tea party are Alice, the Dormouse and this hare.

clue.text: Remarkable reign associated with a queen

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable, able to be marked out afresh, so the letters of reign are rearranged

explanation.surface: A queen's long reign is remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for queen, used in the title of a reigning monarch, as in Elizabeth Regina.

clue.text: Bird in The Muppets

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the words The Muppets

explanation.surface: A bird character appears on The Muppets television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless Australian ratite is a bird.

clue.text: Search round for small jazz band

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone hunts around for a small jazz group to hire.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of musicians, especially in jazz, is informally called this.

clue.text: In lane, aptly off London's Denmark Street?

indicators.note: off means not right or gone bad, so the letters of In lane, aptly are scrambled

explanation.surface: A query asks whether London's Denmark Street fits a lane gone awry.
explanation.walkthrough: The name originally meant New York's songwriting district; London's Denmark Street, famous for music publishers and guitar shops, took the same nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark Street was the centre of British popular music publishing, giving it the American nickname.

clue.text: Cheese wise, before local teams' game?

indicators.note: before says the wise word comes ahead of the game word

parts.note: a sage is wise, and sage is also an adjective meaning wise
a derby is a match between local rival teams

explanation.surface: Is it sensible to eat cheese before a local football match?
explanation.definitionFit: An English hard cheese marbled green with sage leaves is a variety of cheese.

clue.text: Football club magazine

definitions.meaning: the North London Premier League side known as the Gunners
a magazine here is a store of weapons and ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: The Gunners are the North London football club, and a weapons store is a magazine.

clue.text: Artist's abridged title for a villain

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist, and the possessive gives an S

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the last letter of the naming word is cut

parts.note: to title someone is to call them by a name

explanation.surface: A painter's shortened name is given to a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or scoundrel, now often playful, was once a villain.

clue.text: A sailor holding line where knot may be tied

indicators.note: holding means a sailor, as a whole, wraps round the letter for line

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor holds a rope where he can tie a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knot' is not a sailor's knot: to tie the knot is to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples tie the knot, meaning marry, standing at the church table at the front.

clue.text: Harry's horse

definitions.meaning: to harry is to pester, so harries means pesters continually

explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester them, and a worn-out horse shares the same short word.
